title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Jobs saved or created
sections.summary: 155,000 jobs were saved or created, and nearly 2% was shaved off the potential rise in unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One hundred and fifty-five thousand jobs were saved or created.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Nearly 2% shaved off the potential increase in unemployment rate.

sections.label: Unemployment rates compared
sections.summary: Hong Kong's unemployment is 7%, the US 6.3%, and Singapore around 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Hong Kong's unemployment is at 7%, the US at 6.3% while Singapore is around 3%.

sections.label: Support for hard-hit sectors
sections.summary: It asks how the Ministry would support workers in hard-hit sectors, especially if the Jobs Support Scheme ends in September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: How would the Ministry support workers from these hard-hit sectors, especially if the Jobs Support Scheme is slated to end in September this year?

sections.label: Protecting low-wage workers
sections.summary: It asks how many low-wage workers were protected during the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: How many low-wage workers did we manage to protect during this COVID-19 crisis?

sections.label: Care for FDWs
sections.summary: It cites abuse of FDWs, CDE's $200,000 to 1,630 FDWs and support for over 1,500, and asks about future plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over the last few weeks, we have heard unfortunate stories of FDWs being abused.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: NTUC's Centre for Domestic Workers or CDE was set up to help our FDWs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It has disbursed nearly $200,000 to 1,630 of them between 2016 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It has sheltered and supported more than 1,500 of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's future plans to further care for FDWs to prevent unfortunate abuse cases from happening again?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: How can organisations such as CDE complement the Ministry’s work?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I hope that employment agencies can play greater roles in safeguarding the welfare of our FDWs even after a successful placement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Singapore needs MOM to keep its eye focused on implementing our workplace safe management measures right, to implement our employment and workplace safety policies right so that our workers will continue jobs and work safely until Singapore has successfully tackled the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I recently filed a Parliamentary Question and MOM replied that there are at present about 36,000 Professionals, Managers and Executives, or PMEs, earning less than $3,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: If you lower it to $2,600, there are still about 20,000 earning less than $2,600 per month.

sections.label: Non-resident employment fall
sections.summary: Non-resident employment fell sharply in 2020, contracting by 181,500 or 16% year-on-year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In fact, non-resident employment fell sharply in 2020; contracted by 181,500 or 16% year-on-year decrease.

sections.label: Singaporeans placed in jobs scheme
sections.summary: With tripartite partners' support, 76,000 Singaporeans were placed into jobs and skills opportunities under the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: With the support from the tripartite partners, 76,000 Singaporeans have been placed into various jobs and skills opportunities under the scheme.

sections.label: Government commits $5.2 billion
sections.summary: The Government will commit another $5.2 billion to fund this effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government will commit another $5.2 billion to fund this effort.

sections.label: WSG PCP and SkillsFuture support
sections.summary: WSG offers the PCP for mid-career PMETs and SkillsFuture credits, both boosted by the Jobs Growth Incentive's salary co-payment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, currently, WSG offers a Professional Conversion Programme, or PCP, that seeks to enable mid-career PMETs to undergo skills conversion into new occupations or sectors; as well as SkillsFuture credits for all Singaporeans to prepare themselves for potential career transitions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture and the PCP received a further boost under the Jobs Growth Incentive announced in August 2020 where the Government committed to co-pay a quarter – half for those aged over 40 – of the salaries.

sections.label: JGI one-year applicability
sections.summary: The JGI currently applies for up to one year for hires commencing in September 2020 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, the JGI is applicable for up to one year for hires commencing in September 2020 onwards.

sections.label: Question on permanent co-funding support
sections.summary: Given complementarities between the PCP and JGI, the speaker wonders whether co-funding support can be made more permanent.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the inherent complementarities between the PCP and JGI, I wonder whether co-funding support can be made more permanent.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance self-financing system
sections.summary: Redundancy insurance can be made self-financing through workers' contributions and perhaps Government top-up with recurring revenue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of course, they are perennial concerns that have to do with cost, but redundancy insurance can be made a self-financing system heavily supported by workers' own contributions and, perhaps, by some Government top-up with a recurring revenue.

sections.label: Graduate permanent full-time jobs
sections.summary: Recent statistics show fewer graduates found permanent full-time jobs in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Recent statistics indicate that fewer graduates have found permanent full-time jobs in 2020.

sections.label: SG United Traineeship programme progress
sections.summary: The passage asks about the SG United Traineeship programme's progress, permanent employment secured, and plans to expand vacancies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share more about the progress of the SG United Traineeship programme, now that we are more than a year into it?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How many have secured permanent employment from it?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are there plans to expand the programme and create more vacancies across a wider variety of sectors and job roles?

sections.label: Job Sharing Initiative expansion
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will look into expanding the Job Sharing Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry look into expanding the Job Sharing Initiative?

sections.label: Lower skilled elderly employment
sections.summary: The passage states some lower skilled elderly may need to continue employment to sustain independent living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For most Singaporeans, this will, hopefully, be in the form of a good retirement with sufficient savings and restful time to enjoy the company of grandchildren and catching up on hobbies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, this is not necessarily the case for some segments of our lower skilled elderly who may need to continue to hold on to employment in order to sustain independent living.

sections.label: Senior worker grants and CPF rates
sections.summary: The passage mentions 2021 Budget grants, SGUnited programmes, and CPF interest rates of 2.5% and 4%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Despite her goals to be independent and self-sufficient at her age, it did seem that she might have to end up seeking some form of financial assistance in the interim while continuing her uphill job search journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I know that the 2021 Budget has an increase in Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and Part-Time Re-employment Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Also, the SGUnited Skills Programme caters mainly for mid-career jobseekers impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and the SGUnited Traineeship targets mainly fresh graduates from the Institutes of Higher Learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, CPF has been able to maintain its interest rates at 2.5% for Ordinary Accounts and 4% for Special MediSave and Retirement Accounts.

sections.label: CPF dynamic portfolio option
sections.summary: The passage asks whether CPF members can opt a portion of savings for a dynamic portfolio co-invested with Government vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Is there a possibility for CPF members to have similar options where they can opt a portion of their CPF savings for a dynamic portfolio, such as to co-invest with the Government's investment vehicles to enjoy the higher returns.

sections.label: PCP and Capability Transfer Programme
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Professional Conversion Programme and Capability Transfer Programme mitigated pandemic employment challenges and how many PME jobseekers secured jobs through PCP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such I would like to inquire the Ministry on the programmes such as Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) and Capability Transfer Programme have been effective in mitigating the employment challenges faced by Singaporeans during this pandemic?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share to date how many of those PME jobseekers has secured job opportunities through PCP, like the Place and Train, Attach and Train, Job Redesign and Reskilling?

sections.label: Local workforce in Capability Transfer Programme
sections.summary: The Member asks how many of the local workforce have gone through and benefited from the Capability Transfer Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry also share how many of our local workforce have gone through and benefited from the Capability Transfer Programme?

sections.label: Helping Singaporeans and remote work
sections.summary: The Member asks how the Ministry will help Singaporeans leverage these opportunities and minimise job outflow from remote work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry help Singaporeans to leverage on these opportunities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry minimise the outflow of jobs as a result of remote work?

sections.label: Contact-intensive sectors and electronic platforms
sections.summary: Firms in contact-intensive sectors contract and lay off workers without measures like the Job Support Scheme, while some firms selling via electronic platforms do well.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While firms in a contact-intensive sectors suffers a contraction in output and will lay off workers in the absence of policy measures like the Job Support Scheme (JSS), some other firms such as those offering products via an electronic platform do well.

sections.label: JSS and Jobs Growth Incentive
sections.summary: The JSS supports stabilisation by avoiding a cyclical rise in unemployment, while the JGI creates new hires in growth sectors through a hiring subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The JSS provides support to achieve the stabilisation function of the Government, avoiding a cyclical rise in unemployment, while the Jobs Growth Incentive, the JGI package, seeks to create new hires in the potential growth sectors through a hiring subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The JGI is a very important policy measure as it helps to create a good supply of new job vacancies in growing sectors of the economy.

sections.label: Structural transformation in Budget 2021
sections.summary: Pursuing structural transformation as a pillar of Budget 2021, while helping save jobs in the contact-intensive sector, enables the economy to create new job vacancies at trend growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Pursuing structural transformation as a major pillar of Budget 2021, even while help is extended to save jobs in the contact-intensive sector has a virtue of enabling the Singapore economy to create a good supply of new job vacancies when the economy returns to its potential trend growth path.

sections.label: JGI hiring recent graduates
sections.summary: The JGI could encourage firms in growing sectors to hire recent graduates.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The JGI could go some way towards encouraging firms in the growing sectors to hire recent graduates.

sections.label: No combustion engines 2040
sections.summary: With no internal combustion engines by 2040, there will be no petrol stations then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, with no internal combustion engines by 2040, there will not be any petrol stations then.

sections.label: Workforce transition for vulnerable workers
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to update the ITM with workforce transition strategies for low-wage workers, seniors and persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We need to balance and manage this workforce transition, especially when most of the jobs that will be lost are lower wage roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to consider updating our industry transformation roadmap (ITM) to include workforce transition strategies for low-wage workers, seniors and persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Corlison Singaporean workforce training
sections.summary: Over 88% of Corlison's workforce are Singaporeans, and employees above 40 are sent for training at least once every three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More than 88% of Corlison's workforce are Singaporeans and employees above 40 years old are sent on training to acquire new skills at least once every three years.

sections.label: Freelancer union representation protection
sections.summary: The speaker suggests reviewing the Trade Unions Act and employment laws to better represent and protect freelancers, noting own-account workers are 9.7% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As such, I suggest MOM to review the Trade Unions Act to allow freelancers to be union members without compromising or contravening traditional collective bargaining and representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: By the same token, can we also explore ways where our freelancers can be better represented and protected of their fundamental rights as workers through amending existing employment laws such as the Industrial Relations (IR) Act or introducing new legislation to accord them better protection than just what the Small Claims Tribunal and Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) can do at the moment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, based on the MOM's latest 2020 labour statistics, own-account workers, defined as persons who operate their own business or trade without employing any workers – this includes taxi drivers, property agents, tour guides, freelance artists – account for 9.7% of the total workforce, or 228,000 workers, up from 8.8% in 2019.

sections.label: Gig apps and unprotected own-account workers
sections.summary: Aggregated apps like Grab and Deliveroo have increased own-account workers, who are not protected by employment laws or given CPF and benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Such a rise can also be attributed to the advent of aggregated apps such as Grab and Deliveroo, which have provided platforms for people to seek assignments in exchange for monetary incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: We have to recognise that this is a sizable population of the workforce that is not protected by employment laws and regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: These own-account workers are not deemed as employees of companies and the companies are also not obliged to provide CPF, medical insurance and other employee benefits for these people.

sections.label: Gig worker classification rulings
sections.summary: The UK supreme court upheld classifying Uber drivers as workers, and California's Proposition 22 allows partial benefits for gig workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: On 19 February, the UK supreme court has upheld a ruling that Uber's drivers should be classified as workers rather than independent contractors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: California's Proposition 22 ballot measure, passed by the voters in the November elections, could also serve as a third way of classifying such gig economy workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: It allows companies to offer private hire drivers partial benefits such as a minimum base pay that is higher than the minimum wage and healthcare subsidies for some drivers, depending on the number of hours that they work.

sections.label: Standalone minimum wage limits
sections.summary: A standalone minimum wage is too general and does not address sustainability and progression issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A standalone minimum wage is too general and does not address sustainability and progression issues.

sections.label: Hasten PWM implementation
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government and Labour Movement to hasten implementation of PWM in more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As such, I strongly urge the Government and the Labour Movement to further hasten the implemention of PWM in more sectors.

sections.label: Cleaning PWM cost impact
sections.summary: Cleaning PWM could raise dishwashing and cleaning costs, so a targeted approach for smaller enterprises is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For instance, the introduction of cleaning PWM could have increased the cost of dishwashing and cleaning, thereby increasing their operating structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, a targeted approach for smaller enterprises is necessary to keep their business sustainable for themselves and workers, and cost affordable for consumers.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy for enterprises
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to apply the foreign worker levy lever instead of the DRC lever to select enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Noting the above business owners' concerns, I would like to call on the Government to apply the foreign worker levy lever instead of the DRC lever to a very select group of enterprises that are restarting and/or pivoting their existing businesses.

sections.label: Surgical DRC application
sections.summary: Different players in foreign worker-dependent industries have different resources, so DRC should be applied more surgically by sub-sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, different players in the foreign worker-dependent industries, like the food and beverage, and cleaning and maintenance, have different base resources and allure as employment choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, we need to be more surgical in applying DRC in each sub-sector, ensuring that there will be no net increase to the foreign worker population in Singapore based on current DRCs.

sections.label: Manufacturing sector job openings
sections.summary: In November 2020, 6,370 manufacturing jobs were reportedly on offer, with one in 10 from the marine and offshore sub-sector.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In November 2020, there were reportedly 6,370 jobs are on offer in the manufacturing sector, with one in 10 from the hard-hit marine and offshore sub-sector.

sections.label: S Pass foreign worker quota cuts
sections.summary: The S Pass sub-DRC for construction, marine shipyard and process sectors will be cut from 20% to 18% in 2021 and to 15% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The foreign worker quota for S Pass workers in the construction, marine shipyard and process sectors will be cut.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The cuts to the S Pass sub-Dependency Ratio Ceiling, or DRC, is in two phases.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The first tightens the sub-DRC for S Pass workers from 20% to 18% on 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The second step will cut this further to 15% on 1 January 2023.

sections.label: Foreign Employee Dormitories Act coverage
sections.summary: FEDA regulates foreign worker accommodations for health and safety but applies only to dormitories housing 1,000 or more workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Currently, the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act, or FEDA, ensures that the accommodations of our foreign workers are regulated and must comply with a list of requirements to ensure the health and safety of their residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: However, FEDA only applies to larger dormitories that accommodate 1,000 or more workers.

sections.label: New migrant worker dormitory standards
sections.summary: New MOM specifications limit dormitory rooms to 10 single-deck beds with 1 metre spacing, costing operators at least 50% more.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: With new standards for migrant worker dormitories to enhance workers' well-being, dormitory operators said it would see at least 50% higher cost to implement in existing dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Under new MOM specifications, dormitories will have no more than 10 beds per room, with only single-deck beds and 1 metre spacing between them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Each room now holds 12 to 16 beds.

sections.label: Employers penalised for underpaying foreigners
sections.summary: According to MOM, a rising number of employers have been penalised for illegally underpaying foreign employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the MOM, a rising number of employers have been penalised for illegally underpaying foreign employees.

sections.label: Extending FEDA to smaller dormitories
sections.summary: FEDA covers only dormitories housing 1,000 or more workers, and extending it to smaller FCDs will impact over 100,000 more workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: These dormitories are regulated by the Foreign Employee Dormitory Act, or FEDA, which cares for the health and safety of our migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, FEDA presently covers only dormitories that house 1,000 workers and above.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Extending FEDA regulations to the smaller FCDs will impact over a 100,000 more workers.

sections.label: Workers buy catered food
sections.summary: Workers in dormitories without cooking facilities buy catered food costing $120 to $150 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Many workers stay in dormitories without cooking facilities and purchase food from caterers at their own cost, ranging from $120 to $150 a month.

sections.label: Lunch eaten after preparation
sections.summary: Food is prepared as early as 5 pm the day before, so workers eat lunch long after NEA's recommended four hours.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The earliest preparation time we understand is at 5 pm the day before.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thus, our workers eat their lunch long after NEA's recommended time of four hours after food preparation.

sections.label: Levy for workers' lunch
sections.summary: It asks whether part of the workers' levy could fund safe and nutritious lunch for workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: As suggested by some industry caterers, would it be possible for a part of the workers' levy to go into the provision of safe and nutritious lunch for the worker?

sections.label: Employers underpaying foreign employees
sections.summary: About 190 employers yearly were found underpaying foreign employees between 2015 and 2019, close to 1,000 over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister for Manpower, arising from Parliamentary Questions filed by Workers' Party Member of Parliament Mr Faisal Manap and Progress Singapore Party Non-Constituency Member of Parliament Leong Mun Wai, recently confirmed that about 190 employers were found underpaying their foreign employees every year between 2015 and 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That total corresponds to close to 1,000 employers over a five-year period.

sections.label: Raising penalties for underpayment
sections.summary: Underpayment cases rose from 60 errant employers yearly in 2010 to 2014, and raising penalties could deter it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Compared to the numbers from 2010 to 2014 where 60 errant employers each year were found to have illegally deducted the salaries of their foreign workers, the numbers are clearly on the increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One direct way to resolve this matter would be to raise the deterrent effect of the enforcement regime by increasing the penalties for underpayment of foreign workers and Pass holders under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

sections.label: Direct recruitment through testing centres
sections.summary: It asks whether MOM will study establishing direct recruitment channels through licensed Overseas Testing Centres to cut out middlemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOM look into this problem and study the possibility of establishing direct recruitment channels through its licensed Overseas Testing Centres to cut out the middlemen?

sections.label: Migrant worker agency fees
sections.summary: TWC2 found in 2019 that first-time migrant workers, especially Bangladeshi workers, paid average agency fees of $7,606 and median of $7,750.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: In 2019 migrant worker NGO TWC2 found that, for the first-timers, the average agency fee paid, especially for Bangladeshi workers, was $7,606 and the median was $7,750.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: For repeat workers, the average was $4,733 and the median was $4,000.

sections.label: MOM worker application slot cycle
sections.summary: Employers are advised by MOM to apply for a specific date, are told slots are full, and re-apply later, repeating the cycle.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Employers are advised by MOM to apply for workers to endorse a specific date, only to receive replies that the slots are full and to re-apply on a specific later date, with the cycle repeating itself.

sections.label: Daily foreign worker entry slots
sections.summary: The question asks the Ministry to clarify how many daily slots exist for foreign workers entering Singapore and how they are allocated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry clarify how many daily slots are available for entry of foreign workers into Singapore and how these are allocated?

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model for two sectors
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOM for near-future plans for two sectors and to consider implementing the Progressive Wage Model there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: While this is encouraging, I would like to ask MOM what plans they have for these two sectors in the near future and to consider the implementation of the Progressive Wage Model so that more workers benefit from a clear career progression pathway, coupled with the relevant skills, improved productivity and commensurate wages.

sections.label: Lift company maintenance fee increase
sections.summary: A lift company raised maintenance fees over 40%, citing the Progressive Wage Model, but did not say what share would go to workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: One major lift company started with a more than 40% jump in lift maintenance fees, positing that costs would likely rise by 40% on account of the implementation of the Progressive Wage Model in this sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: When this company was questioned what percentage of this increase would go to workers, considering it maintained thousands of lifts across various Town Councils and should benefit from significant economies of scale to accommodate a mandated rise in wages through the PWM, company representatives demurred and argued that a rise in excess of 40% was just an opening position and that this amount was subject to negotiation.

sections.label: Older workers earning under $1,000
sections.summary: MOM data shows over 80,000 citizens and PRs aged 50 and over in other sectors earn under $1,000 monthly, with sector breakdowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based on MOM labour force data, apart from the aforementioned sectors, there are still more than 80,000 Singapore citizens and Permanent Residents aged 50 and over, working in other sectors earning a gross income of less than $1,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These include 27,300 in transportation and storage, 10,900 in public administration and education, 8,000 in manufacturing, 7,400 in health and social services, and, if we include those earning less than $1,500 per month, the numbers more than doubled.

sections.label: PWM expansion to more sectors
sections.summary: The PWM is being expanded to more sectors, including food services, retail, strata management, pest management and solar technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: We have been expanding the PWM to more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I also welcome the recent announcements that PWM will be rolled out to the food services, retail, strata management, pest management, and solar technology sectors.

sections.label: February 2021 workplace fatalities
sections.summary: February 2021 saw 11 workplace deaths in 28 days, compared with 30 fatalities for all of 2020, with smaller construction firms having higher fatality rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: February 2021 – 11 lives were lost at our workplaces in just 28 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This is alarming, if we compare this to the 30 workplace fatalities for the whole of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to MOM’s data, smaller construction firms with less than 50 employees, have a higher fatality rate than larger firms.

sections.label: Employers offering EAP survey
sections.summary: A National Council of Social Services study found fewer than 5% of surveyed employers offered EAP to staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a study conducted by the National Council of Social Services, less than 5% of employers surveyed offered EAP to their staff.

sections.label: Mental Well-being at Workplaces Awards
sections.summary: Tripartite partners will recognise exemplary companies and individuals this year with the Mental Well-being at Workplaces Awards, presented at the annual Singapore WSH Awards Ceremony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: By showcasing the best-in-class and good role models, we can inspire others to follow in their lead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, happy to announce that the tripartite partners have agreed to recognise exemplary companies and individuals this year with the Mental Well-being at Workplaces Awards, which will be presented at the annual Singapore WSH Awards Ceremony.

sections.label: Contract for service workers WICA coverage
sections.summary: Independent contractors under a contract for service, such as couriers, may lack WICA coverage, and the passage asks whether MOM has data on such workers and plans to address their protections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Independent contractors under a contract for service also find themselves in a similar predicament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I have come across Singaporeans undertaking delivery work, like couriers, for example, finding themselves without WICA coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In the event they injure themselves in the course of their work, while loading their vehicles for example, no prospect of Work Injury Compensation exists for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Does MOM have any indication of the number of such workers without WICA coverage, especially those in the low-income bracket?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Separately, does MOM have any plan to address the worker protections for such Singaporean workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: This is in light of developments in other jurisdictions, like the UK, where the Supreme Court recently recognised platform workers as employees, lending weight to important questions over the appropriate statutory protections that should be extended to such workers in future.

sections.label: Labour Movement progressive workplace asks
sections.summary: The Labour Movement asks that, with the Government, employers be encouraged to adopt progressive workplace arrangements, companies be supported in job redesign, and employers be advised on new HR best practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: At the Labour Movement, we ask that, together with the Government, we (a) encourage our employers to open their minds to a new progressive workplace and work arrangements, and, indeed, make these the norm and mainstay in the Singaporean workforce culture; (b) support companies through financial and advisory means the process of job redesign; and (c) advise our employers on the new HR best practices that support the outcomes of the job redesign and flexible work arrangement exercises.

sections.label: FDWs and working women
sections.summary: The speaker says FDWs provide vital care-giving support for working women and cites the abuse death of FDW Piang Ngaih Don.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: In my Budget speech, too, I spoken about how FDWs form a vital care-giving structure for working women and that FDW partners at home allow our working women peace of mind in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: I am sure we are not strangers to the case of 24-year-old Piang Ngaih Don (Pee-eng ngay dong).

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Ms Piang, an FDW from Myanmar, was repeatedly abused to the point of death.

sections.label: Workplace benefits and childcare leave
sections.summary: The speaker asks for workplace benefits for women and notes childcare leave rules differ by children's ages and number.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Understanding and attacking these "moments of truth" could have disproportionate impact on the number of women in our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I ask if the Government could consider more standards on structural workplace benefits, such as nursing rooms, emergency respite care, return-to-work programmes and hiring incentives for women over 40.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to "Choose to Challenge" so that no women will be made to feel the way my residents were made to feel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, while eligible working parents of Singapore citizen children are entitled to six days of paid childcare leave a year, this only applies to children below the age of seven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Parents whose youngest child is between seven and 12 are only eligible for two days of extended childcare leave a year, while childcare leave is held constant, regardless of the number of children a couple has.

sections.label: Eldercare leave as statutory leave
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether eldercare leave, offered by many companies, could be considered a statutory form of leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Many companies have started to offer eldercare leave as an employee value proposition and I would like to ask if this could be considered as a statutory form of leave.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements by employers
sections.summary: The speaker notes 85% of employers offered flexible work arrangements in 2019 and cites UOB and DBS policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: In 2019, about 85% of employers offered some form of formal or ad-hoc flexible work arrangement in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Amongst many companies in Singapore, I note that UOB has already instituted a two-day work from home policy post-COVID-19 while DBS will give its workforce the option to work remotely up to 40% of the time.

sections.label: Women's career and income loss
sections.summary: The speaker says women lose an average of eight years of career and income due to familial care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As Minister of State Gan Siow Huang previously shared, women lose an average of eight years of career and income, often when their careers can be peaking after their thirties, due to familial care.

sections.label: ComCare study on care-givers
sections.summary: The speaker urges a joint MOM and MSF study on long-term ComCare recipients and care-giving obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For low-wage care-givers, I implore MOM and MSF to do a joint study on the recipients of long-term ComCare to examine how many recipients become reliant on financial assistance in their old age due to care-giving obligations in their younger years which kept them from participating in the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The research will help us to project any trends into the future to better understand the reality of our ageing society on low-wage individuals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to take a more data-driven approach towards ensuring better retirement adequacy for the low-wage and sandwiched generation of care-givers and to assess whether a basic income for stay-home care-givers might be a viable and dignified way to distribute social support.

sections.label: Carefare Income Supplement and family care leave
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a Carefare Income Supplement for stay-home care-givers and suggests simplifying childcare and eldercare into a general family care leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As I previously proposed, a "Carefare Income Supplement" will go a long way to support stay-home care-givers, affirming that they play a valued and important role and are not just "calefare" in our society, excuse the pun.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As for PMEs earning higher incomes who also struggle with juggling familial care and work, I would like to suggest simplifying childcare and eldercare into a general family care leave.

sections.label: Parent-care leave for employees
sections.summary: The speaker says a family-friendly Government should introduce parent-care leave for all employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Now we need to be a familyfriendly Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should introduce parent-care leave for all employees.

sections.label: Right to work from home
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOM will look into legislating the right to work from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOM look into legislating the right to work from home?

sections.label: Salary history bans and gender wage gap
sections.summary: The passage cites Boston University research on salary history bans and asks if MOM will consider banning salary history questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In June 2020, researchers at Boston University found that salary history bans in the US led to employers increasing wages for all workers, but especially for women and some racial minorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I quote, “Salary histories appear to account for much of the persistence of residual wage gaps.” Has the Ministry reviewed these studies and whether the declaration of last drawn salary contributes to the gender wage gap here in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOM consider banning questions on salary histories?

sections.label: Support for migrant workers
sections.summary: MOM set up the ACE team, is reviewing expanding FEDA coverage, and will pilot a Migrant Workers' On-boarding Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In August, we set up a new dedicated group in MOM, the Assurance, Care and Engagement (ACE) team, to provide better support to our migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are reviewing plans to expand coverage of the Foreign Employees Dormitory Act (FEDA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: And we will pilot a Migrant Workers' On-boarding Centre.

sections.label: Resident unemployment rate
sections.summary: The passage states that in January, resident unemployment further moderated to 4.3%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In January, resident unemployment further moderated to 4.3%.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive local hires
sections.summary: From September to October 2020, the Jobs Growth Incentive supported over 110,000 new local hires by around 26,000 employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From September to October 2020, we estimate that the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) supported over 110,000 new local hires, by around 26,000 employers.

sections.label: JGI seven-month extension
sections.summary: A seven-month JGI extension is helpful, and what is needed after September will be assessed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: A JGI extension of seven months is helpful, and we will assess what is needed after September.

sections.label: Wage support for jobseekers
sections.summary: Employers get 50% support for the first $6,000 of gross monthly wages for up to 18 months, up to $54,000 per eligible hire.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As noted by Members Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Eric Chua, these jobseekers face greater difficulties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why we will provide 50% support for the first $6,000 of gross monthly wages, for up to 18 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Altogether, employers can receive up to $54,000 for each eligible hire.

sections.label: Higher training allowances for participants
sections.summary: Participants aged 40 and above can receive training allowances up to $3,800, and host organisations share 10% instead of 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Participants aged 40 and above can receive higher training allowances of up to $3,800, compared to $3,000 previously.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Host organisations will share just 10% of the allowance, compared to 20% previously.

sections.label: WSG local job placements
sections.summary: WSG placed close to 55,000 locals into jobs, traineeships and attachments through partnership across Government agencies, unions and employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Thanks to the close partnership across Government agencies, with unions and employers, WSG placed close to 55,000 locals into jobs, traineeships and attachments.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment ages rise
sections.summary: From 1 July 2022, the statutory minimum Retirement Age rises from 62 to 63 and the Re-employment Age from 67 to 68.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We should avoid a disruption of our plans to raise the retirement and re-employment ages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Therefore, from 1 July 2022, the statutory minimum Retirement Age will go up from 62 to 63.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The statutory Re-employment Age will also go up from 67 to 68.

sections.label: Senior Worker Support Package
sections.summary: The government announced a $1.3 billion Senior Worker Support Package last year to give employers fair support for adjustments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: While we are asking more of our employers, we have also provided them fair support to make these adjustments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why we announced the $1.3 billion Senior Worker Support Package last year.

sections.label: Support for senior workers
sections.summary: 1,700 companies with 17,000 senior worker beneficiaries have been supported since July last year, and over $200 million will be topped up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since they started in July last year, we have supported 1,700 companies with 17,000 senior worker beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will top up their budget by over $200 million to directly benefit about 75,000 seniors.

sections.label: Career conversion programmes
sections.summary: Career conversion programmes benefited 12,600 mature individuals in the last three years, and the government wants to go further.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Brother Abdul Samad would be pleased to note that the career conversion programmes benefited 12,600 mature individuals in the last three years, and we want to go further.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: Plans continue to raise retirement and re-employment ages to 63 and 68 from July next year and raise CPF contribution rates for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):    The COVID-19 pandemic has impacted livelihoods and disrupted our lives, but we must continue to press on with some far-reaching policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will continue with our plans to raise the retirement and re-employment ages to 63 and 68 respectively from July next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will also raise the CPF contribution rates for senior workers from January next year to help them accumulate more retirement savings.

sections.label: Employer subsidies topped up
sections.summary: 1,700 companies tapped subsidies to implement new retirement and re-employment ages and part-time roles for 17,000 senior workers, with $230 million topped up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In one year, even with the current COVID-19 outbreak, 1,700 companies have tapped government subsidies to bring forward their plans to implement the new retirement and re-employment ages, as well as create part-time roles, to help 17,000 senior workers remain in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To encourage and support more employers, the Ministry of Manpower has decided to top up $230 million for the two subsidies.

sections.label: SEPs in labour movement
sections.summary: Collectively, about 47,500 SEPs are already part of the labour movement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Collectively, about 47,500 SEPs are already part of the labour movement.

sections.label: Lean scheme and local salary
sections.summary: An average of 20,800 firms benefited annually from the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme, and further Local Qualifying Salary increases are held off this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the last three years, an average of 20,800 firms benefited annually through the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, periodic adjustments will continue to be made to the Local Qualifying Salary, to ensure that locals are not hired on a token salary in order to access foreign worker quota.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will hold off further increases this year to give firms time to recover from the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: S Pass manufacturing quota cut
sections.summary: The S Pass sub-DRC in Manufacturing will be reduced gradually from 20% to 18% next year and to 15% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As mentioned by the Deputy Prime Minister in his Budget speech, we will also reduce the S Pass sub-DRC in Manufacturing gradually, from 20% to 18% next year, and to 15% in 2023.

sections.label: Foreign workforce and 2020 contraction
sections.summary: The foreign workforce accounted for all of Singapore's employment contraction in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Whatever her criticism, the foreign workforce accounted for all of our employment contraction in 2020.

sections.label: CTP extension and funding
sections.summary: About $5 million has been committed under CTP, employers co-fund part of costs, and it will be extended to September 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The CTP remains a useful complement to sector-specific schemes, as well as broad-based schemes like LEDS and JGI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have committed about $5 million so far under CTP, and employers have to co-fund part of the costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As announced, we will extend it to September 2024.

sections.label: DP holders need work pass
sections.summary: From 1 May 2021, Dependant's Pass holders who wish to work in Singapore will be directed to apply for a relevant work pass.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 1 May 2021, DP holders who wish to work during their stay in Singapore will be directed to apply for a relevant work pass, such as an EP, S Pass or Work Permit.

sections.label: Jobs Transformation Maps funding
sections.summary: Close to $10 million will be set aside over two years for more Jobs Transformation Maps, with three completed and 12 planned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: WSG supports these through existing Professional Conversion Programmes, as well as the new Place-and-Train programme for Supply Chain and Logistics Coordinators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will set aside close to $10 million over the next two years for more of such Jobs Transformation Maps (JTMs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Three JTMs have been completed and we have plans for another 12.

sections.label: Job redesign and local hiring support
sections.summary: Subsidies, employment agencies and P-Max help companies hire and place local workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They bridge the knowledge gaps for companies to develop and implement job redesign solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This year, we raised the subsidy to 80%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Close to 31,000 SME employers have benefited the JGI and SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will help companies looking for local talent to also get professional assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We recently appointed five best-in-class employment agencies under a new Human Capital Partnership programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They help employers consider talented locals they may sometimes overlook, by focusing on their transferable skills and relevant experience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We also have the P-Max programme which has placed over 7,800 PMETs into 7,300 SMEs in the last five years.

sections.label: Job Security Council help
sections.summary: Its Job Security Council helped many workers retain their jobs or move into new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Its Job Security Council helped many workers retain their jobs or move into new jobs.

sections.label: Global COVID-19 infections and deaths
sections.summary: Over 114 million people worldwide have been infected and more than two million have died.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As of today, over 114 million individuals all over the world have been infected and more than two million have died.

sections.label: CMP workforce shrinkage in 2020
sections.summary: In 2020, the construction, marine and process workforce shrank by about 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In 2020, the construction, marine and process or CMP workforce has shrunk considerably, by about 15%.

sections.label: CMP worker testing and SHN
sections.summary: On-arrival tests and a seven-day post-Stay-Home Notice test extend CMP workers' Stay-Home Notice to 21 days.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We introduced on-arrival tests and an additional post-Stay-Home Notice seven-day testing process for CMP workers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This essentially means that the Stay-Home Notice (SHN) for these workers has been extended to 21 days.

sections.label: Migrant Worker Onboarding Centre
sections.summary: A Migrant Worker Onboarding Centre has been set up to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To do so, we have set up a Migrant Worker Onboarding Centre (MWOC).

sections.label: CMP workers' 21-day requirements
sections.summary: Higher-risk CMP workers serve 21 days, with a residential onboarding programme including medical examination and orientation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: All other CMP sector workers from higher risk countries are now required to serve 21 days – first 14-day SHN plus another additional seven-day testing process as a further precaution.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At the MWOC, while the workers are undergoing the additional seven-day testing process, they will also go through a residential onboarding programme, comprising: one, the enhanced medical examination; and two, the orientation and the SIP that I have alluded to earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, workers above the age of 40 or with risk factors will also be screened for chronic illnesses like diabetes, high blood pressure and high cholesterol.

sections.label: Residential settling-in programme
sections.summary: The residential settling-in programme teaches new migrant workers dormitory living, worksite practices, employment rights, health practices and social norms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The residential settling-in programme will inculcate better dormitory living and worksite practices amongst migrant workers who have just arrived here and help them understand their employment rights, the kind of good health practices and Singapore's social norms.

sections.label: Migrant worker dormitory distribution
sections.summary: Of 280,000 migrant workers in dormitories, 60% stay in 50 large FEDA-regulated dormitories and 40% in FCDs, CTQs and TOLQs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Sixty percent of the 280,000 migrant workers in dormitories stay in just 50 large dormitories with beds of 1,000 or more and they are regulated under the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act (FEDA).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Forty percent of them are in the numerous FCDs, CTQs and TOLQs.

sections.label: Reviewing FEDA scope expansion
sections.summary: The pandemic highlighted the need to strengthen regulatory levers, so the scope of FEDA is being reviewed to cover all dormitories regardless of size.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our experience in containing this pandemic in the dormitories highlighted the need to strengthen our regulatory levers in order to enable us to raise and enforce housing standards very quickly across the various dormitory types and sizes, and to introduce new housing standards to make dormitory living more resilient to public health risks.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are thus reviewing the scope of FEDA to expand it to cover all dormitories, regardless of size.

sections.label: Regulatory framework review timeline
sections.summary: Feedback will be incorporated into the regulatory framework details, with the review hoped to be completed in the second half of 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will consider the details of the regulatory framework by incorporating their feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We hope to complete this review and provide more details in the second half of 2021.

sections.label: Quick Build Dormitories rollout
sections.summary: Since September 2020, over 25,000 beds have been rolled out in Quick Build Dormitories, with each room capped at 10 residents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Since September 2020, we have progressively rolled out over 25,000 beds in Quick Build Dormitories (QBDs).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, the capacity in each QBD room is capped at 10 residents.

sections.label: PBD operating model study
sections.summary: The Government is studying developing upcoming PBDs on a different operating model from the current system of releasing land for commercial operators to bid, build and operate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government is studying the possibility of developing the upcoming PBDs on a different operating model compared to the current system, where land is released for commercial operators to bid, to build and to operate.

sections.label: Assurance, Care, Engagement Group
sections.summary: Since August 2020, the Assurance, Care, and Engagement (ACE) Group has been set up.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Since August 2020, we have set up the Assurance, Care, and Engagement (ACE) Group.

sections.label: Migrant worker medical services
sections.summary: About 200 workers daily use the 24-hour telemedicine service via the FWMOMCare app, and about 500 workers a day receive medical support for non-acute ARI and chronic conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Today, about 200 workers use the 24-hour telemedicine service available to them via the FWMOMCare app on a daily basis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have piloted 13 regional medical centres and further increased access by opening a night clinic in each of the West, Central and East regions of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: About 500 workers a day receive medical support for non-acute respiratory illness (ARI) conditions like gastritis or chronic diseases like diabetes.

sections.label: Migrant worker medical insurance review
sections.summary: MOM is reviewing medical insurance coverage for migrant workers to help employers manage medical expenses and give employers and workers greater peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: MOM is reviewing medical insurance coverage for migrant workers to help employers better manage their medical expenses, and to give both employers and workers a greater peace of mind.

sections.label: Migrant worker volunteer network
sections.summary: ACE will tap existing volunteer networks to set up migrant worker volunteers in every dormitory with 100 or more residents, and offer para-counselling training for peer support and mental health.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, ACE will tap on existing volunteer networks, such as MWC’s volunteer ambassadors for a start, to set up a network of migrant worker volunteers in every dormitory with 100 or more residents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Second, we will offer para-counselling training to our migrant worker volunteers to encourage peer support and better protect the mental health of our migrant workers.

sections.label: Errant employers salary cases
sections.summary: Between 2015 and 2019, 950 errant employers were caught for not paying contractual fixed monthly salary or inflating salaries, affecting about 1,400 foreign employees.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2019, 950 errant employers were caught for not paying the foreign employees their contractual fixed monthly salary or inflating the salaries with no intention of paying them the amount that has been declared.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: There were about 1,400 foreign employees affected in these cases.

sections.label: Electronic payment for migrant workers
sections.summary: As of January 2021, over 97% of employers pay migrant workers in dormitories electronically.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As of January 2021, more than 97% of employers pay their migrant workers living in the dormitories electronically.

sections.label: Recruitment fee limits and enforcement
sections.summary: Laws cap EA recruitment fees at one month's salary per contract year, capped at two months, with refunds and enforcement penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our laws limit the recruitment fees charged to migrant workers by Employment Agencies (EAs) in Singapore at one month of their salary for each year of their contract, capped at two months.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: EAs must also refund 50% of the recruitment fee to the worker if the employment is terminated within six months and MOM takes strong enforcement actions against EAs that do not comply with these requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: MOM also actively takes enforcement action against persons performing EA activities without an EA licence, or engaging in hiring activities without an agent licence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Such persons face a jail term of up to two years or a fine of up to $80,000, or both.

sections.label: Reporting employment issues, illegal agents
sections.summary: Workers are urged to report employment issues early; illegal employment agent activities decreased in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We continue to encourage and we hope that you would help us to send the message out as well, to ask them to come forward early to report if they face any employment-related issues.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: There was a decrease in illegal employment agent activities in 2019, with around 70 foreigners and 18 Singaporeans being taken to task, compared to an average of over 100 foreigners and 25 Singaporeans per year in the preceding three years.

sections.label: Recreation Centre visits increased
sections.summary: From this month, migrant workers can visit Recreation Centres up to three times a week on rest days or after work.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Starting from this month, instead of once a week – which means in early March, instead of once a week – migrant workers can visit the Recreation Centres up to three times a week, on their rest days or after working hours.

sections.label: Testing, tracing devices, community visits
sections.summary: Workers must have attended rostered routine testing and carry contact tracing devices; plans are being drawn for monthly community visits.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To mitigate transmission risk from inter-mixing, these workers must have attended their rostered routine testing and they must continue to carry their contact tracing devices.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are also currently drawing up plans to allow eligible workers to visit the community once a month.

sections.label: Future outbreak response capabilities
sections.summary: Plans include a Migrant Worker Onboarding Centre pilot and expanding the Foreign Employees Dormitory Act to all dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Going forward, we will help migrant workers and migrant worker dormitories to enhance their capabilities to respond to future outbreaks in three key areas: First, we will fortify our first line of defence by putting in place preventive measures before and when migrant workers arrive in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will pilot a Migrant Worker Onboarding Centre, or MWOC – an end-to-end onboarding process that will integrate the Stay-Home Notice (SHN) and on-arrival testing, for all Construction, Marine and Process (CMP) sector work permit and S Pass holders entering Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Second, we will strengthen the resilience of our dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We intend to expand the Foreign Employees Dormitory Act (FEDA) to cover all dormitories, including those with fewer than 1,000 beds.

sections.label: Preventive measures investment savings
sections.summary: The Government believes investing in preventive measures today will save future spending on managing outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government believes that investing in these preventive measures today will save us from spending more in the future to manage future outbreaks.

sections.label: Workfare eligibility in 2020
sections.summary: In 2020, about 440,000 people were eligible for Workfare if they earned under $2,300 monthly and met other criteria.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In 2020, about 440,000 people were eligible for Workfare, as long as they earned less than $2,300 a month and met all other eligibility criteria.

sections.label: Workfare Special Payment support
sections.summary: Last year the Government gave low-wage workers a one-off $3,000 cash Workfare Special Payment, benefiting about 500,000 workers with $1.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To cushion the impact on the incomes of low-wage workers, last year, the Government assisted them with the one-off Workfare Special Payment of $3,000, fully in cash, on top of regular Workfare payouts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In total, approximately 500,000 Singaporean workers benefited from about $1.5 billion of Workfare Special Payments.

sections.label: PWM basic wage floor increase
sections.summary: To mitigate reduced overtime wages, tripartite partners agreed to a $150 increase in the PWM basic wage floor, double preceding years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To mitigate the impact of reduced overtime hours on wages, the tripartite partners agreed to a $150 increase in the PWM basic wage floor, double that in preceding years.

sections.label: PWM extension to food retail
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup agreed to extend the PWM to food services and retail, potentially covering up to 80,000 local workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As we strive to emerge together from the pandemic, I am pleased to announce that the Tripartite Workgroup has agreed to extend the PWM to the food services and retail sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: These sectors are among the sectors with the largest numbers of low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We estimate that these PWMs could cover up to 80,000 local workers.

sections.label: Cleaner and security officer wage growth
sections.summary: Because of the PWM, cleaners' median gross monthly wages grew 37% to $1,388 in 2019, and security officers' 29% to $2,391.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In good part because of the PWM, the median gross monthly wages of cleaners have seen cumulative real growth of 37% since 2013, to $1,388 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For security officers, we saw cumulative real growth of 29% since 2015 to $2,391 in 2019.

sections.label: Wage growth for bottom 20%
sections.summary: Real wages for the bottom 20% rose 39% from 2009 to 2019, and at P10 by 37%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The bottom 20% of wages increased by 39% in real terms in the last decade, 2009 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: At P10, we are just increased by 37% in real terms – same period.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model coverage
sections.summary: PWMs benefit 85,000 workers, coverage will at least double to 218,000, with aspiration to cover all sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the PWMs currently benefit 85,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In the short term, we will be at least doubling the coverage up to 218,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: More importantly, it remains our aspiration to cover all sectors with Progressive Wages in the longer term, on top of Workfare as the fundamental layer of support for all our low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Workgroup expects to conclude its deliberations and issue its recommendations to Government to do so before the end of the year.

sections.label: Lift technicians' median wages
sections.summary: Median gross monthly wages for full-time resident lift technicians rose from about $3,300 in 2017 to about $3,800 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: First, since introducing PWM for the sector through Government procurement in 2019, we have seen median gross monthly wages for full-time resident lift technicians rise from around $3,300 in 2017, to about $3,800 in 2019.

sections.label: Main contractors' safety responsibility
sections.summary: Main contractors must ensure overall worksite safety including sub-contractors, and MOM launched CheckSafe in January.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Main contractors must also be responsible for ensuring overall safety across their worksites, including managing the safety performance of sub-contractors on their sites.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To motivate both main and sub-contractors to improve their workplace safety practices, MOM launched the CheckSafe e-service in January this year to make construction companies' safety track records readily available.

sections.label: Prosecuting main contractors, safety framework
sections.summary: MOM will prosecute main contractors failing safety duties for sub-contractor workers, and will release a safety framework for public tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For construction fatalities involving sub-contractors' workers, we will also prosecute the main contractor if they fail in their duty to ensure safety of workers on the site.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Later this year, MOM will release a framework emphasising safety performance for public sector construction tenders.

sections.label: WSH Act maximum penalty
sections.summary: The maximum penalty for WSH Act offences increased from $250,000 in 2016 to $400,000 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty for WSH Act offences have increased from $250,000 in 2016 to $400,000 in 2019.

sections.label: Graduate employment and traineeship extension
sections.summary: About nine in 10 IHL graduates who entered the labour force last year found jobs or traineeships within six months, and the SGUnited Traineeships Programme is extended to 31 March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: About nine in 10 graduates from our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) who entered the labour force last year found jobs or traineeships within six months of graduation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Traineeships Programme will be extended by an additional year till 31 March 2022.

sections.label: Traineeship training allowance increase
sections.summary: Training allowance rises about 30% for ITE graduates up to $1,800 and about 20% for Polytechnic graduates up to $2,100.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To facilitate this, the training allowance for ITE graduates will increase by about 30%, up to a maximum of $1,800 and about 20% for Polytechnic graduates, up to a maximum of $2,100.

sections.label: Shorter maximum traineeship duration
sections.summary: The maximum traineeship duration has been shortened from nine to six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The maximum traineeship duration has been shortened from nine to six months.
